prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system, through PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as my preferred prize, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. It is a new chemical modality whose mechanism is understood at the molecular level: a designed small molecule brings a ubiquitin ligase and a chosen protein together, and independent laboratories have confirmed this through ternary-complex structures, cooperativity and degradation kinetics. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC principle; Handa identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which explains how glue degraders work and which brings an approved class of drugs (lenalidomide, pomalidomide) into the same ubiquitin-ligase logic. One citation about redirecting the ubiquitin-proteasome system can honestly cover both strands. I did not change my configuration in round 2; what changed is that I now hold it more firmly, because the objections raised against it concern timing and attribution, not the science.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader is approved, so the therapeutic payoff of the PROTAC half is not yet shown, and I weigh that as a real risk to timeliness, not as a disqualifier. Attribution is hard: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim made decisive contributions that a three-name limit omits, and the citation must be worded so it does not imply that these people did not matter. Whether PROTACs and glues are one discovery or two is a legitimate question; I treat them as one because both rely on induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, but a committee that reads them as two would find the single citation too broad.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Ciulli as the third name because VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned PROTACs into a general, drug-like platform, and regards cereblon as target identification in a single drug class.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my configuration and I weighed it seriously. I still decide for Handa on one criterion: the Nobel test is a discovery that changed understanding, and identifying cereblon as the target is that kind of result, since it explained a half-century-old drug and then explained why lenalidomide and pomalidomide work. Ciulli's work is excellent engineering that generalised an existing concept. If the citation is narrowed to PROTACs only, Ciulli becomes the better third name; because I want the glue strand in the citation, I keep Handa. I could accept Ciulli, and I would not treat it as a reason to change my vote on B023 itself.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B002 first as mature and overdue, regards B023 as early, and sees PROTACs and glues as two mechanistically separate strands, with cereblon emerging from thalidomide biology and not rational design.
responses.response: I accept that B002 is the safer prize and that attribution is cleaner. Where I disagree is on the glue strand: that cereblon came from thalidomide biology and not from design does not make it a separate discovery, because the Nobel tradition has often honoured the explanation of a mechanism. Your point that C-N coupling differs from the 2010 C-C chemistry persuades me, and I list B002 as an alternative for that reason, but I weigh the novelty of a new modality above the delay in recognising a mature method.

responses.point: Zou keeps B002 first but says she moved B023 up after reading the ballots; her reservation is that PROTACs and cereblon glues may be two discoveries and that Ciulli, Gray and Ito are comparable to the third name chosen.
responses.response: I welcome that your reservation is about attribution and not about the science. On the question the chair put to you both, I think the clinical status differs between the strands: the glue half already has years of approved use in myeloma, so only the bifunctional half lacks approval. I would regard a two-part prize as artificial and would not propose it. I understand you hold B002 on principle, and I do not read your Kosugi caveat as a reason to move; I would expect the citation for B002 to be worded around general C-N coupling.

responses.point: Chabes argues that approved glue drugs give clinical validation, that Handa should come before Ciulli, and asks whether B028 has a settled credit split among Meyer, Mayer, Nocera and Hammes-Schiffer.
responses.response: I agree with the Handa argument. On B028, I cannot say that the credit problem is settled. A single sentence would be that proton-coupled electron transfer is a general mechanism linking proton and electron movement in enzymes and catalysts, but the people credited developed it in different settings: theory, physical-organic thermochemistry and molecular electrocatalysis. A defensible three-name set would be Nocera, Mayer and Hammes-Schiffer, with Meyer's priority a real objection, so I keep it only as an alternative and I disclose that my own field is close to it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads PROTACs and cereblon glues as one achievement, since a narrow reading would make Ciulli the better third name.
Whether the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader makes the prize premature this year.
Whether B028 has a defensible three-name set; my proximity to the field means I cannot judge this without bias.
statement.conflict_note: I work on proton transfer and biological energy conversion, close to B028 (PCET), so I discount my own opening first place for it; B028 appears only as an alternative. I am a Stockholm University colleague of committee member Xiaodong Zou, who is not a candidate. I have no tie to any person in the B023 configuration and see no conflict requiring recusal.
